description: This course covers the fundamentals of programming for cybersecurity, focusing on secure coding practices, vulnerability analysis, and incident response. Topics include secure programming techniques using Python and C, common software vulnerabilities such as buffer overflows and SQL injection, and the use of OWASP ZAP for penetration testing. The course also explores cryptographic algorithms like AES and RSA, secure communication protocols such as TLS, and the implementation of secure authentication mechanisms using OAuth 2.0. Students will learn to analyze and mitigate security risks in code, design secure systems using secure coding standards, and implement security testing tools for real-world applications.

clos.text: Define secure coding practices and their role in preventing common software vulnerabilities such as buffer overflows and SQL injection.
Describe the principles of cryptographic algorithms like AES and RSA, and their application in securing data transmission and storage.
Explain the operation of secure communication protocols such as TLS and their importance in ensuring data integrity and confidentiality.
Apply secure programming techniques in Python and C to develop code that mitigates vulnerabilities and adheres to OWASP guidelines.
Implement security testing tools such as OWASP ZAP to perform penetration testing and identify vulnerabilities in web applications.

topics: Common software vulnerabilities and their exploitation
